title: Holding Back a Share of the Month's Credits on a Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
The money credited to a Keyturn Host Payout Account in the month up to that day, counting the earnings and the corrections booked in that month, is the base from which a share is held back until the statement closes. That base is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

The share of that month's credits held back turns on whether the host has already drawn in the month and on whether the month's entries have been corrected.

1. **Where a transfer has already been released from the account in the month up to that day**, half of that month's credits is held back, that is 50 percent of them.
2. **Where no transfer has been released from it in that month and a correcting entry has been booked to it in that month**, none of that month's credits is held back, the share standing at 0 percent.
3. **In every other case**, a quarter of that month's credits is held back, that is 25 percent of them.

The sum held back is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## How the two tests interact

The first test is whether a transfer has already been released in the month up to that day. Where one has, the first case governs whatever the corrections show. Only where none has is the second test asked: a correcting entry booked to the account in that month puts it in the second case, and the absence of one leaves it in the third.

## On hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical account credited with 2000.00 USD of earnings and 400.00 USD of corrections in the month up to that day, so that the month's credits come to 2400.00 USD. The sum held back is 1200.00 USD in the first case, 0.00 USD in the second and 600.00 USD in the third.
